analysis:
All three changed files are test-only: ScheduledWindowSelectionTests.swift (new test at lines 130-192), AutopilotAdoptionTests.swift (new) and AutopilotBusyReasonTests.swift (new). No production source, wire protocol, key handling, attestation, or cache storage code is changed, so no threat-model assets or boundaries are directly altered by this diff.

The tests encode security-relevant expectations about production behavior that were not visible in this batch:
- Adopted inventory keeps serving without a lease, while unadopted inventory is withdrawn and refused with model_not_selected.
- Adoption is revoked on unload, consent revocation, disable, deselection, self-test failure, retiring, weight-hash unavailable, and shutdown (AutopilotAdoptionTests lines 104-141).
- Without consent, the snapshot omits the capabilities, adopted, held and busy fields (lines 160-173).
- Carried-over cached builds are kept only while their weight hash still matches, and are dropped when rewritten or vanished (ScheduledWindowSelectionTests lines 134-192). This relates to T-012/T-027 weight integrity.
- Busy-reason detail is withheld once consent is revoked (BusyReasonTests lines 104-113).

The tests use test-only ProviderLoop extensions that mutate internal state, such as autopilotControl = nil, failedSelfTestHashes and busy flags. These live in the test target, so they add no production attack surface. The production implementation (adoption, withdrawal, snapshot gating, ScheduledWindowSelection.noteAutopilotCachedBuilds) was not supplied. Whether the production code matches these test expectations is therefore unverified; that is a coverage limit, not evidence of a regression. I raise no findings. A later pass on the non-test source files should confirm the weight-hash recheck on carry-over, withdrawal of adoption on every basis end, and consent-gated disclosure of busy detail.
